one_liner: Embeddable RISC-V full-system and userland emulator with a tracing JIT; claims, without numbers, to outrun QEMU TCG.
what_it_does: Emulates RV64/RV32 IMAFDCB machines (Zkr, Zicbom, Zicboz, Sstc) with SMP, PCIe, NVMe, RTL8169 networking, framebuffer, VFIO passthrough and AIA/PLIC interrupt controllers, and boots OpenSBI + U-Boot, Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD and Haiku guests. It ships as the rvvm command-line VM (QEMU-like flags such as -m, -smp, -i) and as librvvm, a C library API for creating multiple machines per process, writing devices (PCI, MMIO, DMA, IRQ) and running RISC-V thread contexts inside a host process (userland emulation, work in progress). It is not a drop-in for QEMU: the device model, image formats and command line differ, and it emulates RISC-V guests only.
how_it_is_fast: RVJIT is a trace-based dynamic binary translator. The interpreter runs guest code and, when it misses in a per-hart JIT TLB, records the instructions it executes (interpret-trace-compile) into a block keyed by physical PC, unrolling through JAL up to a size cap and turning AUIPC+JALR pairs with known targets into direct exits. Guest registers are mapped to host registers with an LRU allocator. Exits to blocks in the same 4 KiB page are patched into direct jumps (block chaining), while cross-page exits do an inline lookup so self-modifying-code invalidation stays per page (dirty-page bitmaps). Floating point is not JIT-compiled; the interpreter runs it on the host FPU, switching host rounding modes, instead of QEMU-style soft-float emulation.
when_to_use: Running or embedding a full RV64 Linux/BSD/Haiku guest on an x86-64, ARM64 or RISC-V64 host, where RVJIT is enabled by default
Products that need a RISC-V VM as a library: librvvm is MPL-2.0 and supports static linking into non-GPL code, with JNI bindings
FP-heavy guest code where a hardware-FPU interpreter path beats soft-float emulation (the author's only figure is about 10x on synthetic FPU benchmarks, search snippet only)
Sandboxed emulation on Linux or OpenBSD hosts: seccomp or pledge isolation plus a privilege drop to nobody
when_not_to_use: If you need measured evidence: no RVVM-vs-QEMU benchmark, workload, hardware or QEMU version is published anywhere the verifier or this pass could reach
Guests that need the Vector extension (RVV) or RVA23-class profiles: USE_RVV defaults to 0 and vectors are a TODO

Code that depends on bit-exact IEEE behaviour of fused multiply-add under directed rounding: issues #306 to #310 (opened 2026-09-06, still open) report wrong results and flags in the software FMA fallback used on x86-64 hosts without the builtin FMA path
Hosts without a JIT backend (WASM, DOS, i386 or arm32 for 64-bit guests) fall back to the interpreter, which the wiki calls slower
Production setups that need QEMU's breadth: virtio devices are on the TODO list, KVM is work in progress, and userland emulation is marked WIP

integration.form: shared lib or static lib (librvvm) plus the rvvm and rvvm-user executables; GNU Make (recommended) or CMake build
integration.dependencies: none required (libm for the FPU); optional X11, Wayland or SDL for the GUI and a sound backend; libraries can be probed at runtime
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler; the wiki lists GCC, Clang, cosmocc and TCC as compiler brands; LTO on by default; exact minimum C standard not documented
integration.platforms: Hosts: Linux, *BSD, macOS, Windows, Haiku, also WASM and DOS (no JIT). JIT backends: x86_64, ARM64, RISC-V64 (default), with a LoongArch64 header in src/rvjit and legacy i386, arm32 and riscv32 backends that can only accelerate riscv32 guests
integration.thread_safety: Multiple machines per process are supported. Each hart owns its own JIT cache, and dirty-memory marking is atomic across harts; other API thread-safety rules are not documented.

gotchas: The 'faster than QEMU TCG' claim has no numbers, workloads, hardware or QEMU version anywhere in the README or wiki; the only figure (about 10x on synthetic FPU benchmarks) is the author's HN comment, seen as a search snippet only.

The hardware-FPU path, which the wiki credits for the speed, still has open correctness bugs. The software FMA fallback (src/util/fpu_lib.h, used on x86-64 hosts without the optimal builtin FMA) gives wrong results under directed rounding (#309 reports 173 differences in 4,000 directed-mode cases for fmadd.s) and corrupts inf/NaN inputs (#306). RMM rounding is mapped to host round-to-nearest-even with a separate fix-up step.
When the JIT code cache fills, the whole per-hart cache and its links are flushed (no partial eviction). Caches are not shared between harts ('shared caches' is a TODO), so memory grows with -smp.
The default branch is 'staging', and the README asks bug reporters to check staging; the last tagged version shown is 0.7-git.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick RVVM over rv32emu or rv8 when you need a full-system RV64 machine (NVMe, PCIe, networking, GUI) that boots stock Linux/BSD images and can be embedded as an MPL-2.0 library. rv32emu has an actual benchmark against QEMU v9.0.0 but targets RV32. For a sandboxed RISC-V scripting engine inside an app, libriscv is the closer fit.
verified_claims_summary: No measurement exists: the README and wiki only assert 'Faster than QEMU TCG', crediting the tracing RVJIT IR, less splitting of guest instructions and use of the host FPU. The one figure is the author's informal 'about 10x with some synthetic FPU benchmarks' (search snippet only), with no hardware, compiler or QEMU version.
status_note: Very active (2,926 commits on the staging branch, last commit 2026-10-05 per the verified record, 45 open issues, many of them recent FPU-conformance reports with fix PRs pending). librvvm is MPL-2.0, so it is usable as a vendored library; the rvvm and rvvm-user binaries are GPL-3.0.
